ignoreValues.reason: custom-pointer, highlight-image, and skip-link are decorative/utility elements meant to stay viewport-bound (overflow-x:clip on html/body was added specifically to prevent them causing horizontal scroll); site has no tooltip/menu/popover anywhere that this could clip

Same rationale as the prior stylesheet: body{overflow-x:clip} exists specifically to stop fixed/absolute utility elements (loader overlay, back-to-top button, skip-link) from causing horizontal scroll. None of them are tooltips/menus/popovers -- this site has none -- so there's nothing for the clip to wrongly cut off.

Verified against actual CSS, not assumed: .work-list/.work-entry declare no padding of their own, but the nested .work-entry a (the real text-bearing element) has padding:2rem 0 -- 32px, well above the 8-16px floor -- which is what actually renders; detector isn't tracing padding through to a descendant. .section/.section-ink padding is clamp(4rem,3rem+5vw,8rem) clamp(1.25rem,1rem+2vw,3rem) -- 64-128px/20-48px -- real and substantial; likely a clamp()/custom-property resolution limit in the static check. Confirmed comfortable spacing in live screenshots both cases.
